To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) polymorphic worms are often vulnerable to signature based intrusion detection and (2) we can automatically generate signatures for polymorphic worm payloads.
we have developed a system that automatically generates signatures for polymorphic malware.

(i) we have identified classes of signatures that match polymorhpic worms with low false positives and negatives, (ii) we have developed algorithms that automatically generate signatures in these classes, (iii) we have evaluated these algorithms on a large range of polymorphic worm variants and found that they produce signatures that match the worms, and (iv) we have implemented a prototype of Polygraph and evaluated it on a range of real-world worms.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of signature generation for polymorphic worms; and our contributions are algorithms for signature generation, a signature generation framework, and an evaluation of our algorithms on a range.
the design of a content signature generation system for polymorphic worms, the design of a new class of signature for content based IDS, and the evaluation of these algorithms in practice.
the following question: can a content signature based intrusion system successfully detect a polymorphic worm?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithms for automatic signature generation for polymorphic worms is a very promising approach, and that it can be successfully implemented and deployed in practice.
our work demonstrates that polymorphic worms can indeed be matched using signature based IDS.
Polygraph can be used for automatic generation of polymorphic worm signatures with low false negatives and low false positives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Polygraph is a practical and effective solution for the problem of polymorphic worm detection.
Polygraph is the first signature generator that can automatically generate signatures for polymorphic payloads, and that these signatures exhibit very low false negatives and low false positives.
Polygraph is able to generate signatures that are able to detect polymorphic worm variants with 100% detection rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polymorphic worms are not as stealthy as is widely assumed.
content signatures are still a viable defense against polymorphic worms.
polymorphic worms can be detected with a content-based signature, and that such detection can be done in a scalable manner.
